decisionRules: Never choose a UDC number solely by keyword similarity.
Use the most specific verified class available in the supplied Abridged/reference dataset.
Do not add an auxiliary merely because it is possible; add it only when the document content/form and the schedule justify it.
Use + for coordinated non-consecutive subjects, not as a generic multi-topic separator.
Use / only for a consecutive extension/range supported by the schedule; do not substitute +.
Use : for a simple relation; use :: only when order-fixing is required.
Use [ ] only when subgrouping is required to preserve the intended scope of a compound expression.
Language, form, place, human ancestry/ethnic grouping/nationality, time and general-characteristic auxiliaries are common auxiliaries and must be validated against the relevant table.
Special auxiliaries are local to their designated subject area and must never be copied from another class.
For ambiguous titles, request more information instead of fabricating a number.
Separate subject from document form. Words such as dictionary, handbook, atlas, bibliography or textbook do not automatically become the main subject.
For literature, distinguish language/linguistics from literature and literary form from physical/document form.
For history/geography, distinguish subject, place and time; add place/time only when supported by the title or description.
Preserve exact punctuation and decimal notation in the final UDC expression.
